proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(E_0\) for \(E_{P_{0,O}}\), and put \(G_b=\sum_xg_{b,x}\).  First consider PT.  Since \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\mathbf 1_J=0\), differentiation of
\[
 q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x)
\]
after allowing an arbitrary derivative of the latent scalar \(\delta_1^0(x)\) gives
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot D(x).
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus the latent derivative has disappeared, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) says precisely that the Riesz representer of (1) is \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\).  The symmetric idempotent matrix \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has null space \(\operatorname{span}(\mathbf 1_J)\), hence matrix rank \(J-1\).  Therefore the Gram rank of the displayed statistical representers is at most \(J-1\).  It is exactly \(J-1\) under the additional nondegeneracy condition stated in the corrected claim.  The qualification is necessary: if all donor outcomes are conditionally constant, the mean derivatives, and hence the corresponding Riesz representers, can vanish even though \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) itself has matrix rank \(J-1\).

We next identify the observed tangent spaces rather than assuming them.  In the PT branch the observable restriction is \(r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)=0\).  Conversely, any observed law satisfying these equal-donor-change equations has a compatible PT full-data extension: conditionally on \((G=1,X=x)\), choose an unobserved \(Y_T(0)\) whose mean is \(\mu_{1,T-1}(x)+\Delta\mu_2(x)\), retain all observed coordinates, and impose the already assumed no-anticipation equalities before \(T\).  In the SC branch, full column rank of \(B(x)\) makes \(w(x)=\{B(x)'B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)'a(x)\) unique and smooth.  The equation \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0\) is equivalent to \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\).  Conversely, an observed law satisfying this equation has an SC full-data extension obtained by choosing the unobserved treated-group \(Y_T(0)\) to have conditional mean \(w(x)'(\mu_{2,T}(x),\ldots,\mu_{J+1,T}(x))'\).  Hence, locally, the observed projections of the two full-data branches are exactly the zero sets of their displayed finite moment maps.

For a score \(s\) of a branch submodel, differentiating \(r_{b,x}=0\) and using Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) gives
\[
 E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0\quad\text{for every }x.
 \tag{2}
\]
For the reverse inclusion, retain a maximal independent row system of the derivative of \((r_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X)\).  The locally constant-rank hypothesis permits a nonsingular coordinate minor.  Given a bounded score in the kernel in (2), exponentially tilt the observed law by that score and by one bounded score for each retained row.  Solving the finitely many equations \(r_{b,x}=0\) for the latter coefficients uses that nonsingular minor; differentiating the equations at zero shows that all correction coefficients have derivative zero because (2) holds.  Thus the resulting restriction-preserving path has the prescribed score.  Truncating and recentering an arbitrary \(s\in L_0^2(P_{0,O})\), and applying the same finite-dimensional correction before taking the \(L^2\) limit, proves
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)=\bigcap_{x\in\mathcal X}\ker\{s\mapsto E_0[R_{b,x}s]\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The full-data extensions in the preceding paragraph show that these corrected observed paths are induced by paths in the required causal branch.

Because there are finitely many rows, (3) and elementary Hilbert-space duality give
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)^\perp=\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) gives \(E_0[G_bs]=\dot\theta_b(s)\) for unrestricted scores.  Therefore Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}influence\text{-}classes}\), followed by (3)--(4), yields
\[
 \mathcal I_b(P_0)=G_b+\mathcal T_b(P_0)^\perp
 =G_b+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Finally stack the retained rows in \(R_b\), let \(\Gamma_b=E_0[R_bR_b']\), and let \(u_b=E_0[R_bG_b]\).  The orthogonal projection of \(G_b\) on the finite-dimensional row span is \(R_b'\Gamma_b^\dagger u_b\).  Hence the minimum-norm element of the affine set (5) is
\[
 \phi_b=G_b-R_b'\Gamma_b^\dagger u_b.
 \tag{6}
\]
The Moore--Penrose identities show that (6) is unchanged by redundant displayed rows, completing the proof.

We first verify identification, keeping the causal target separate from the two observed-law functionals.  Under no anticipation, all observations before \(T\) equal untreated potential outcomes, and donor observations at \(T\) are untreated.  If PT holds, then for every \(x\) and every donor \(g\),
\[
 \delta_1^0(x)=\Delta\mu_g(x).
\]
Consequently the conditional treated effect is the treated observed final change minus \(J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J'D(x)\), and averaging with the treated-stratum weights \(p_X(x)p_1(x)/\pi_1\) proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_O)\).  If SC holds, full rank identifies \(w(x)\) from the preperiod equations and its final-period equation gives
\[
 E_F[Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]=\sum_{g=2}^{J+1}w_g(x)\mu_{g,T}(x).
\]
Subtraction from the observed treated mean and the same treated-stratum averaging prove \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_O)\).  Thus the two observed functionals agree at every intersection law; neither equality is definitional.

For one stratum define
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)=g_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}'a,
 \qquad
 \psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=g_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}'d.
 \tag{1}
\]
The affine normal form in \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\) says that sums of the first functions in (1) exhaust the PT influence class, and sums of the second exhaust the SC influence class.  To see directly that their intersection is nonempty, note that \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0\) and the intercept row of \(a=Bw\) imply \(\mathbf 1_J'w(x)=1\).  The PT normal span therefore permits replacing the uniform donor average in the PT gradient by the weights \(w(x)\).  Suppressing for one line the common treated-stratum factor \(p_X(x)p_1(x)/\pi_1\), call the resulting bracket
\[
 F_x=\mu_{1,T}-\mu_{1,T-1}-w'(\mu_{2,T}-\mu_{2,T-1},\ldots,
 \mu_{J+1,T}-\mu_{J+1,T-1})'.
\]
On the SC restriction set, the last preperiod matching equation is
\(\mu_{1,T-1}=w'(\mu_{2,T-1},\ldots,\mu_{J+1,T-1})'\), so \(F_x\) equals the SC final-level bracket there.  After restoring the common treated-stratum factor, the two stratum contributions agree; because their bracket difference is zero at \(P_0\), differentiation of that factor contributes zero to their derivative difference.  Hence the difference of their unrestricted derivatives annihilates the SC tangent space and, by the normal form, is an SC-normal linear combination.  The gradient of the weighted \(F_x\) contribution therefore has both representations in (1).  This supplies a feasible pair for every stratum and proves nonemptiness without presuming it.

By the definition of \(h_x\),
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=c(a,d)'h_x.
\]
Because \(\Omega_x=E_0[h_xh_x'\mid X=x]\) is positive semidefinite,
\[
 \Omega_x^{1/2}c(a,d)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 E_0[(c(a,d)'h_x)^2\mid X=x]=c(a,d)'\Omega_xc(a,d)=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus the constraint of \(\mathrm{QP}_x\) is exactly equality in \(L^2(P_{0,O}\mid X=x)\) of the two influence-function representations.  Its objective is
\[
 E_0[\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)^2\mid X=x]
 =\ell_{\mathrm{PT}}(a)'\Omega_x\ell_{\mathrm{PT}}(a).
 \tag{3}
\]
Functions belonging to different strata have disjoint support and each stratum has positive mass by \(p_X(x)\ge\kappa_0>0\).  Therefore minimization of the unconditional squared norm separates over strata.  Equations (2)--(3) prove
\[
 \phi_U=\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^U)
       =\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^U),
 \qquad
 V_U=\sum_xp_X(x)\min\mathrm{QP}_x.
 \tag{4}
\]
Singularity causes no ambiguity: all coefficient minimizers selected by the program represent the same minimum-norm function, and the Euclidean minimum-norm tie rule merely chooses coordinates.  The spectral-gap condition ensures stability of those retained coordinates but is not used to manufacture feasibility.

An estimator regular on the union is regular along every quadratic-mean differentiable submodel in each branch.  Its derivative covariance equations must therefore hold on both tangent spaces, so its regular influence component lies in \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\).  Applying the convolution lower-bound result in \(\mathrm{lem{:}semiparametric\text{-}convolution\text{-}bound}\) and then (4) gives asymptotic variance at least \(\|\phi_U\|_{P_0}^2=V_U\).  The cited Sun--Xie--Zhang result \(\mathrm{lem{:}sun\text{-}xie\text{-}zhang\text{-}branchwise\text{-}laws}\) supplies separate PT and SC limit variances; (4) instead is the sharp lower bound imposed by regularity with respect to both branch tangent sets at an intersection law.  This proves the stated strengthening.

Use the notation \(\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)\) and \(\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)\) from the proof of \(\mathrm{thm{:}union\text{-}envelope}\).  By the tangent normal form and the definition of the oracle coefficients,
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^{\mathrm{or}}),
 \qquad
 \phi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^{\mathrm{or}}).
 \tag{1}
\]
Disjoint stratum support and \(p_X(x)>0\) imply
\[
 \|\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}-\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\|_{P_0}^2
 =\sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x^{\mathrm{or}})'
   \Omega_xc(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x^{\mathrm{or}}).
 \tag{2}
\]
The right side is the simultaneous Gram discrepancy.  It is nonnegative and is zero exactly when the two canonical gradients are equal in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\).

Let \(A=\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\), \(B=\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\), and \(C=A\cap B\).  These are closed affine subsets of a Hilbert space: their direction spaces are finite spans of restriction normals.  The union theorem proves \(C\ne\varnothing\), and \(C\subseteq A\).  Since the squared norm is strictly convex as a function of the represented Hilbert-space element, its minimizer on \(A\) is unique.  It follows that
\[
 V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in C
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in B.
 \tag{3}
\]
The final condition in (3), using (1) and the normal form for \(B\), is equivalent to the existence of \((d_x)_x\) for which
\[
 \sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x)'\Omega_xc(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x)=0.
\]
The finite-dimensional minimum is attained, including in singular designs after redundant rows are removed, so this is exactly zero PT-oracle discrepancy.  Interchanging PT and SC proves
\[
 V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \min_{(a_x)}\sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x,d_x^{\mathrm{or}})'\Omega_xc(a_x,d_x^{\mathrm{or}})=0.
 \tag{4}
\]
Finally, simultaneous equality implies by (3)--(4) that both branch canonical gradients equal the unique minimum-norm element of \(C\), and hence equal each other.  Conversely, if \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\), that common function belongs to \(C\) and is no larger in norm than any member of \(C\), so all three bounds coincide.  Equation (2) proves the equivalent simultaneous Gram test.  Every entry of the displayed programs is a conditional second moment of the observed-data vector \(h_x\), so the tests are observed-law functionals.

There is one stratum, and all three group probabilities equal \(1/3\), so cell mass and overlap hold because \(\kappa_0<1\) and \(\epsilon_0<1/3\).  No anticipation holds by construction.  The three untreated final changes are all zero.  Hence conditional PT holds and
\[
 D=(0,0)',\qquad \delta_1^0=0,\qquad
 q_{\mathrm{PT}}=\delta_1^0\mathbf 1_2-D=(0,0)'.
 \tag{1}
\]
The two donor columns of the preperiod matrix and the treated target are
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\\-2&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B'B=\begin{pmatrix}6&-4\\-4&6\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The eigenvalues of \(B'B\) are \(2\) and \(10\), so the SC rank condition holds because \(\kappa_0<1\).  Solving \(Bw=a\) gives the unique weights \(w=(1/2,1/2)'\).  These weights reproduce the treated untreated mean in all three periods, establishing the synthetic-mean restriction.  Together with the moment-envelope premise, (1)--(2) prove \(P^\star\in\mathcal M_I\).  The qualification by that premise is indispensable: under the displayed Rademacher construction the largest untreated/control fourth moment equals \(68\), while the treated observed final fourth moment equals \((\tau^\star)^4+6(\tau^\star)^2+1\); an arbitrary positive value of \(M_4\) need not dominate them.

Let \(z_{g,t}=3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\varepsilon_{g,t}\), the influence function of the corresponding cell mean.  The nine variables \(z_{g,t}\) are pairwise orthogonal.  Their variances, ordered by time within groups, are
\[
 (3,3,3),\qquad (3,3/2,3/2),\qquad (6,6,6).
 \tag{3}
\]
In particular the donor final-change influence functions have variances \(3\) and \(12\).  The PT normal changes the donor weights while preserving their sum.  Writing those weights as \((v,1-v)\), the part of the PT variance affected by this choice is
\[
 3v^2+12(1-v)^2.
\]
Its derivative is \(30v-24\), and its second derivative is \(30>0\); hence the unique PT-efficient weights are \((4/5,1/5)\).  The treated-change contribution is \(6\), so
\[
 V_{\mathrm{PT}}=6+3(4/5)^2+12(1/5)^2=\frac{42}{5}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The PT restriction contrast has positive variance \(15\), and \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has rank one, so the profiled PT normal has rank one.

For completeness, we compute the SC face and not merely its final coefficients.  A vector orthogonal to both columns of \(B\) is \(u=(0,-2,1)'\), with \(u'u=5\).  At the restriction, differentiating least squares gives
\[
 dw=(B'B)^{-1}B'(da-dB\,w),
 \qquad
 -(-2,2)dw=(0,-2/5,-4/5)(da-dB\,w).
 \tag{5}
\]
Thus the unrestricted SC gradient has coefficients, by group and time,
\[
 (-2/5,-4/5,1),\qquad(1/5,2/5,-1/2),\qquad(1/5,2/5,-1/2).
 \tag{6}
\]
Normalize the single SC normal as
\[
 \rho=u'(da-dB\,w).
\]
Adding \(\beta\rho\) to (6), the preperiod variance is, using (3),
\[
 Q(\beta)=3(-2/5-2\beta)^2+3(-4/5+\beta)^2
 +3(1/5+\beta)^2+\frac32(2/5-\beta/2)^2
 +6(1/5+\beta)^2+6(2/5-\beta/2)^2
 =\frac{207}{8}\beta^2+\frac35\beta+\frac{99}{25}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Hence the SC oracle coefficient is \(\beta^{\mathrm{or}}=-4/345\), and \(\min Q=91/23\).  The final-period variance in (6) is \(3+(3/2)/4+6/4=39/8\), so
\[
 V_{\mathrm{SC}}=\frac{39}{8}+\frac{91}{23}=\frac{1625}{184}.
 \tag{8}
\]

Every SC influence function has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\), because its normals use preperiod coordinates only.  Equality with a PT representative therefore forces the PT donor weights to be \((1/2,1/2)\).  Matching (6) to that PT representative then forces \(\beta^U=-1/5\): its treated preperiod coefficients become \((0,-1)\), each donor's become \((0,1/2)\), and its final coefficients are \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\).  Thus the common influence function is the equally weighted DiD score and
\[
 V_U=6+3(1/2)^2+12(1/2)^2=\frac{39}{4}.
 \tag{9}
\]
The unequal pairs \((1/2,1/2)\ne(4/5,1/5)\) and \(-1/5\ne-4/345\) show respectively that the PT- and SC-oracle gradients do not lie on the other affine face.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}adaptation\text{-}frontier}\), both one-sided discrepancies are positive.  Numerically and exactly,
\[
 V_U-V_{\mathrm{PT}}=\frac{27}{20}>0,
 \qquad
 V_U-V_{\mathrm{SC}}=\frac{169}{184}>0.
 \tag{10}
\]
All matrices and variances in (2)--(10) depend continuously on cell probabilities, means, and second moments while the positive eigenvalues and cell probabilities stay away from zero.  Strict inequalities are open conditions.  Intersecting their neighborhood with \(\mathcal M_I\) and the fourth-moment envelope gives the claimed relatively open region.

If \(J=1\), then \(\mathbf 1_J\mathbf 1_J'=1\), and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\) gives
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}=I_1-1=0,
 \qquad r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=0.
 \tag{1}
\]
The tangent normal form therefore gives \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)=\mathcal H_{P_0}\) and makes \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\) a singleton, whose element is \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\).  Every SC tangent score is also an unrestricted observed-data score.  At an intersection law the two observed identifying functionals equal the same causal ATT, so their derivatives agree on every SC tangent score.  It follows that \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\), whence
\[
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0),
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)
 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Definitions of \(\phi_U,V_U\) now give \(\phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\) and \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}\).

For the final comparison set \(T=2\), write \(\Delta Y=Y_2-Y_1\), \(m_g(x)=E_O[\Delta Y\mid G=g,X=x]\), and note that \(p_2(x)=1-p_1(x)>0\) by overlap.  Differentiating the observed PT functional gives
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}(O)
 =\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=1\}}{\pi_1}\{\Delta Y-m_1(X)\}
 -\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=2\}}{\pi_1}\frac{p_1(X)}{p_2(X)}\{\Delta Y-m_2(X)\}
 +\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=1\}}{\pi_1}\{m_1(X)-m_2(X)-\theta\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Each residual in (3) has conditional mean zero; the final term accounts for changes in the treated covariate distribution and centers the expression, so direct pathwise differentiation verifies (3).  Formula (3) is exactly the panel-data ATT efficient influence function identified by the cited Proposition 1 in \(\mathrm{lem{:}santanna\text{-}zhao\text{-}panel\text{-}did\text{-}gradient}\), after translating its treated and comparison indicators to \(G=1\) and \(G=2\).

Fix a branch \(b\) and a nearby \(P\in\mathcal M_b\).  By the tangent normal form,
\[
 \mathcal I_b(P)=\sum_xg_{b,x}(P)+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}(P):x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The coefficients \(a_x^U(P_0)\) and \(d_x^U(P_0)\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}score\text{-}extension}\) are fixed finite vectors.  Substitution in (1) proves \(\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P;b,P_0)\in\mathcal I_b(P)\).  At \(P=P_0\), the two formulas are the two equal representations selected by \(\mathrm{QP}_x\); the union theorem therefore gives
\[
 \phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_0;\mathrm{PT},P_0)
 =\phi_U(P_0)
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_0;\mathrm{SC},P_0).
 \tag{2}
\]

It remains to prove the rate rather than assert continuity.  The QMD condition and its bounded score norm imply
\[
 \left\|\sqrt{dP_{n,O}/dP_{0,O}}-1\right\|_{L^2(P_{0,O})}=O(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{3}
\]
For a cell indicator times \(Y_t^k\), \(k=0,1,2\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the factorization of the difference of the two densities gives
\[
 |E_{P_{n,O}}f-E_{P_{0,O}}f|
 \le
 \left\|\sqrt{dP_{n,O}/dP_{0,O}}-1\right\|_2
 \left\{E_{P_{n,O}}[f^2]+E_{P_{0,O}}[f^2]
 +2(E_{P_{n,O}}[f^2]E_{P_{0,O}}[f^2])^{1/2}\right\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The fourth-moment envelope makes the second factor bounded, and cell mass and overlap permit division by all relevant cell probabilities.  Hence every cell probability, conditional mean, and conditional second moment entering \(g_{b,x}\), \(R_{b,x}\), and \(\Omega_x\) differs from its value at \(P_0\) by \(O(n^{-1/2})\).

The inverse \((B'B)^{-1}\) is locally Lipschitz because its least eigenvalue is at least \(\kappa_0\).  Likewise, after retaining the fixed independent coordinates, inversion on the nonzero Gram eigenspace is locally Lipschitz because \(\lambda_{\min}^+(\Omega_x)\ge\kappa_0\) and rank is constant.  The finite-cell influence formulas are affine in the observed residuals with coefficients that are smooth functions of the moments just listed.  Equations (3)--(4) and the second-moment bound therefore imply, for either chart,
\[
 \|\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_n;b,P_0)-
   \phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_0;b,P_0)\|_{L^2(P_{n,O})}
 =O(n^{-1/2}).
 \tag{5}
\]
When both labels are admissible, subtract (5) for the two branches and use the common center equality (2).  The triangle inequality yields
\[
 \|\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_n;\mathrm{PT},P_0)-
   \phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_n;\mathrm{SC},P_0)\|_{L^2(P_{n,O})}
 =O(n^{-1/2}),
\]
as required.  All constants may depend on the fixed sequence's QMD score bound; the lemma does not claim a supremum over sequences.

theorem.statement: Under the frozen definition of \(\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\), the requested uniform asymptotic-linear conclusion, and hence the requested four-part affirmative attainment result, is false in general. In particular, at \(P_0=P^{\star}\) for fixed margins that admit the witness with slack, finite-coordinate splicing produces two elements of \(\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\) having the same observed law at their \(n\)-th coordinates but different admissible chart labels, while the normalized empirical sum of the two chart extensions has variance bounded away from zero. No single estimator can have both expansions uniformly. The assumptions permit sequencewise local claims only; a genuine uniform theorem requires a common local neighborhood, a common bound on the QMD scores and remainders, and exclusion of arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.
theorem.proof_tex:
The obstruction comes from the quantifiers in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}union\text{-}sequences}\), not from failure of the center QP.  Choose the allowable constants so that \(P^\star\) satisfies the moment and spectral margins with strict slack.  For a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta\ne0\), construct another intersection law by retaining the donor means and all innovation laws of \(P^\star\), and replacing the treated untreated mean path by
\[
 (1/2+\delta)(-1,-2,-2)+(1/2-\delta)(1,2,2)
 =(-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta).
 \tag{1}
\]
Give its treated final outcome the same fixed additive treatment effect.  Both donor changes and the treated untreated change remain zero, so PT holds.  The unique SC weights are now \((1/2+\delta,1/2-\delta)\), so SC also holds.  By continuity, for sufficiently small \(|\delta|\) all strict support, moment, rank, spectral, and variance margins remain valid.

Call this perturbed law \(Q_\delta\).  For every integer \(m\), form two triangular sequences.  In each, set the law at index \(m\) equal to \(Q_\delta\) and set the law at every other index equal to \(P^\star\).  Give the \(m\)-th coordinate label PT in the first sequence and SC in the second; use any admissible label elsewhere.  Each sequence belongs to \(\mathfrak L_U(P^\star)\): after its one exceptional coordinate it is identically \(P^\star\), so the QMD display holds with score zero and zero remainder eventually, and every coordinate obeys the fixed margins.  Thus, when an infimum or supremum is taken over all sequences separately at each sample size \(m\), its \(m\)-th coordinate includes both labeled copies of \(Q_\delta\).  This is the finite-coordinate-splicing defect.

At \(P^\star\), the witness calculation shows that the common score uses final donor weights \((1/2,1/2)\).  Hence the PT chart extension, whose normal coefficient is frozen at \(P^\star\), still has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\) at \(Q_\delta\).  An SC normal has only preperiod coordinates, whereas the unrestricted SC gradient at \(Q_\delta\) has final donor coefficients \((-1/2-\delta,-1/2+\delta)\).  Therefore
\[
 \Delta_\delta(O):=
 \phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^\star)(O)
 -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^\star)(O)
\]
has final-innovation component \(\delta(z_{2,3}-z_{3,3})\).  Independence of the preperiod and final innovations yields
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 \ge \delta^2\{\operatorname{Var}(z_{2,3})+\operatorname{Var}(z_{3,3})\}
 =\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
 \tag{2}
\]
The two putative uniform expansions at sample size \(m\), applied to the two spliced sequences, have the same left side because both the data law \(Q_\delta\) and the causal target are identical.  Subtraction would force
\[
 m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta_\delta(O_i)=o_{Q_\delta}(1)
 \tag{3}
\]
uniformly as \(m\to\infty\).  But the left side of (3) has the strictly positive variance in (2) for every \(m\).  Moreover \(\Delta_\delta\) is a bounded linear combination of the Rademacher innovations, so the fourth moments of these normalized sums are uniformly bounded.  Convergence in probability to zero would then, by uniform integrability of their squares, force their variances to converge to zero, contradicting (2).  Thus no estimator can satisfy the requested uniform asymptotic-linear expansion.  Since that expansion is one conjunct of the requested construction, the full affirmative conclusion, including variance and multiplier assertions tied to it, is impossible under the frozen sequence class.  This argument does not rule out a sequencewise result or a result after replacing the class by a uniformly quantified local neighborhood.

added_lemmas.statement: In a quadratic-mean differentiable semiparametric model, the limiting law of any regular estimator of a pathwise differentiable scalar parameter is the convolution of the centered normal law whose variance is the squared norm of the canonical gradient with an independent remainder law; in particular, its convolution variance is no smaller than that squared norm.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) satisfying the displayed rank conditions, profiling the \(J\)-coordinate map \(q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x)\) over the unrestricted path of \(\delta_1^0(x)\) yields the observed normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\) for \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\). Its displayed coordinates have Gram rank at most \(J-1\), and the rank is exactly \(J-1\) whenever \(E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{\mathrm{PT},x}R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}]\) has rank \(J-1\). For either branch, \(\mathcal T_b(P_0)=\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{b,x}s]=0\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\) and \(\mathcal I_b(P_0)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}\). Consequently, \(\phi_b=\sum_x g_{b,x}-R_b^{\prime}\{E_{P_{0,O}}[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\}^{\dagger}E_{P_{0,O}}[R_b\sum_xg_{b,x}]\), with redundant PT and SC rows handled by the Moore--Penrose inverse.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The matrix \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has rank \(J-1\), but the Gram rank of its statistical Riesz representers can be smaller when donor outcomes are conditionally degenerate. The frozen assumptions impose no lower variance bound that forces rank \(J-1\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose that the constructed law \(P^{\star}\) obeys the displayed fourth-moment envelope, that is, \(\max_{1\le g\le3}\max_{1\le t\le3}E_{P_O^{\star}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]\le M_4\). Then the corrected PT vector is \(q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=(0,0)^{\prime}\), its profiled normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has rank one, and \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\). The uniquely identified SC weights are \((1/2,1/2)\), while minimizing the PT Gram criterion over donor weights summing to one gives inverse-change-variance weights \((4/5,1/5)\). The union QP therefore fixes the final donor coefficients at \((1/2,1/2)\); its required SC preperiod-normal coefficient differs from the SC oracle coefficient, so both one-sided Gram discrepancies are strictly positive. Hence \(V_U>\max\{V_{\mathrm{PT}},V_{\mathrm{SC}}\}\). The same inequalities hold on a relatively open region preserving the fourth-moment envelope, full rank, unequal positive donor-change variances, and unequal SC and PT-oracle weights.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Membership in \(\mathcal M_I\) includes the fixed fourth-moment bound. The constructed Rademacher law has maximum untreated/control fourth moment \(68\) and treated observed final fourth moment \((\tau^\star)^4+6(\tau^\star)^2+1\), so it is not in the model for an arbitrary positive \(M_4\). Conditioning on the displayed envelope is a necessary regularity restriction, not the efficiency crux.

proposed.statement: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\), the common class \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\) is nonempty, and every estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) has convolution variance at least \(V_U(P_0)=E_{P_{0,O}}[\phi_U^2]\). If \((a_x^U,d_x^U)\) solves \(\mathrm{QP}_x\) built from the profiled \(J\)-coordinate PT normals and the SC normals, then \(\phi_U=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\}\), and \(V_U\) is the sum of the stratum program values weighted by \(p_X(x)\). This strictly strengthens SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, at intersection laws by replacing its two branch-specific asymptotic variances with the sharp convolution bound for estimators regular under PT-or-SC uncertainty.
proposed.justification: The theorem identifies the efficiency price of not knowing which nonnested identifying restriction is correct and makes that price computable by finite covariance algebra.
proposed.gap: SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, proves pointwise asymptotic and bootstrap laws separately under PT and SC; TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010, Section 3, attains intersection efficiency for a different finite-support odds-ratio union, but provides no PT--SC restriction-normal program or ATT convolution bound.
proposed.consumer: RummoEtAl2026 can replace branch-contingent precision claims in its short-panel sugary-drink-tax comparison with the sharp variance envelope that remains valid when PT or synthetic comparison supplies identification.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the causal-identification, support, convolution-bound, and comparator facts used directly by the proof.

proposed.statement: At \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\), simultaneous oracle adaptation holds if and only if the observable simultaneous Gram discrepancy in \(\mathrm{def{:}oracle\text{-}gram\text{-}tests}\) is zero; equivalently, \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\) if and only if \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\) in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\). One-sided PT adaptation \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}\) holds if and only if the PT-oracle Gram discrepancy is zero, and one-sided SC adaptation \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\) holds if and only if the SC-oracle Gram discrepancy is zero. These are finite covariance-matrix tests in \(\Omega_x\), \(a_x^{\mathrm{or}}\), and \(d_x^{\mathrm{or}}\), all identified from the observed law.
proposed.justification: Necessary-and-sufficient criteria distinguish genuine oracle adaptation from accidental equality of reported standard errors.
proposed.gap: TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 establishes local efficiency at one intersection model, whereas no cited result gives simultaneous and one-sided iff adaptation criteria for two nonnested ATT branches with different restriction derivatives.
proposed.consumer: An applied analyst can diagnose from estimated derivative constraints whether identification robustness is asymptotically free in a particular short-panel design.

proposed.statement: When \(J=1\), \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}=0\), so profiling the sole treated-versus-donor equality leaves no PT observed-data normal and the PT observed-law tangent space is unrestricted. At every intersection law the full-rank SC observed model is therefore locally nested in the PT observed model, \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\), \(\phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\), and \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}\). With \(T=2\), this PT gradient equals the panel-DiD ATT efficient influence function in SantAnnaZhao2020, Proposition 1.
proposed.justification: This reduction checks that the new envelope collapses to the established two-group panel-DiD bound when union geometry disappears.
proposed.gap: SantAnnaZhao2020 gives the two-group panel-DiD bound but does not derive it as the nested special case of a PT-or-SC union envelope.
proposed.consumer: The reduction provides a benchmark against the maintained two-period DiD routines already used by empirical researchers.

proposed.statement: Under the constant-rank conditions, \(\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P;b,P_0)\in\mathcal I_b(P)\) for every \(P\in\mathcal M_b\) in a neighborhood of \(P_0\), and \(\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_0;\mathrm{PT},P_0)=\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(P_0;\mathrm{SC},P_0)=\phi_U(P_0)\). Along every \(((P_n,b_n))\in\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\) for which both chart labels are admissible, the \(L^2(P_{n,O})\) distance between the PT and SC extensions is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).
proposed.justification: The lemma supplies a branch-valid and center-coherent score on PT-only and SC-only local sequences, so the attainment target never invokes an intersection-only object off the intersection.
proposed.gap: SunXieZhang2025 gives separate branch scores, but does not construct a fixed-rank continuation from their common intersection score into both local charts.
proposed.consumer: The chart extension is the score target needed for one branch-robust interval under local switching in the Alaska and sugary-drink-tax panels.
